prompt: What are some interesting things about elevator mechanics
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 provides a largely correct, general overview of elevator mechanics (counterweight/traction concepts, safety systems, maintenance, and emergency response) with few or no clearly fabricated specifics. Candidate 2 contains multiple implausible or incorrect technical claims (e.g., bamboo-fiber elevator ropes, rooftop wind turbines powering elevators, and very specific historical/ratio assertions) that significantly reduce correctness. Candidate 3 is the most error-prone, with several major false statements about counterweights, speeds, cable materials/lifespans, and brake mechanisms. Candidate 4 is moderately inaccurate: some ideas are plausible (braking and counterweight roles), but other details are oversimplified or unlikely (e.g., “GPS-based” stopping precision, machine-room-at-bottom generalization, and hydraulic operation “without any cables at all”).
